clue.text: Made a comeback, having banked without pressure

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the depending word wraps round the pressure symbol

parts.note: banked on means relied on
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone recovered after leaning on support, minus any pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: RELIED goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply is to answer back, so a retort is a comeback.

clue.text: Frustrate officers learning in school

indicators.note: in places the officers' training group inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: OTC, the Officers' Training Corps, is where officers learn

explanation.surface: Military cadets studying at a school get thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Officers' Training Corps is a British university cadet unit; 'learning' makes it read like a description of officers at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to put an end to it, thwarting it.

clue.text: Throw vegetable over ridge

indicators.note: throw over here means flip end to end, so the vegetable's letters run backwards
over completes the phrase throw over, the sign that the word is turned round

parts.note: a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: Tossing a vegetable over a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A keel is the long ridge along a ship's bottom, or a bird's breastbone crest.

clue.text: Dog (setter) taken round a group of islands sheltered by dam

indicators.note: something sheltered by the dam sits inside its letters

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun is wrapped round the islands

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A dog, maybe a setter, is walked around an archipelago behind a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: '(setter)' looks like a breed of dog beside 'Dog', but it is the crossword setter referring to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weimaraner is a grey German gundog breed.

clue.text: Wet weather reportedly raised grass for animal

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for wet weather is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: rain is wet weather

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, reads the grass word from bottom to top

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands

explanation.surface: Rainy conditions are said to have made grass grow for some beast.
explanation.walkthrough: RAIN sounds like REIN; REED turned upwards by 'raised' gives DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is an Arctic deer, one example of an animal.

clue.text: Dear result of failing to score in the sack?

indicators.note: in puts the zero score inside the word for the sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
love is a score of nil in tennis, the result of not scoring

explanation.surface: A risque quip about striking out romantically in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to score' looks like a romantic failure in bed, but love is simply nil in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beloved is cherished, held dear, much as a darling is.

clue.text: One who might give lines would turn to betrayal if given them

indicators.note: the answer would become the betrayal word if given the lines, so those letters come out of it

parts.note: treachery is betrayal
them refers back to lines, and RY (railway) stands for lines

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher handing out lines might turn traitor if handed lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add R and Y (railway lines) to the answer and you get TREACHERY. Lines are also a school punishment, writing a sentence over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster may set lines, a punishment of copying out a sentence many times.

clue.text: Judge about to release European on the inside

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: on the inside puts the European letter within the release word

parts.note: to free is to release

explanation.surface: A magistrate is set to let a European inmate go.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee adjudicates a game, acting as its judge.

clue.text: By which we should not forget passionate email or otherwise

definitions.text: By which we should not forget

parts.note: warm means ardent, passionate

indicators.note: otherwise says the letters of the two words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A heated email is easy to recall, or not.
explanation.definitionFit: A war memorial is a monument so that the fallen are remembered.

clue.text: Collection to feed everyone provided backing for many boats

indicators.note: to feed puts the collection word inside, like food into a mouth
backing reads the joined words for everyone and provided from right to left

parts.note: all means everyone
if means provided
a lot is a collection of items at auction

explanation.surface: Gathering enough to feed everyone, if it gets support, for a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns both words at once, giving FILLA; 'to feed' then puts the collection inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a fleet of small ships.

clue.text: Film star for whom Rome is a fair clue

definitions.text: Film star for whom Rome is a fair clue

parts.words: Film star for whom Rome is a fair clue
parts.note: Rome sits inside the star's surname letters, with only the N and O to spare, so the city name hints fairly at the blonde star

explanation.surface: Suggesting a city name as a reasonable hint for a movie actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' also nods to the actress's famous blonde hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn of that surname was a famous Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Write back to cut relative

indicators.note: back says the writing word is read in reverse

parts.note: to pen is to write
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Penning a reply to cut off a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family relation of that kind.

clue.text: My name's written inside boot, extremely briefly

indicators.note: written inside places the name abbreviation within the boot word

parts.note: a wellie is a rubber boot (a wellington)
N is an abbreviation for name

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter off the word for extremely

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: Someone's name is inked inside their boot, very briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation of surprise. WELLIE is British for a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of astonishment, as in 'My!' or 'Well, I never!'

clue.text: International company needs to yield in foreign seas

indicators.note: in places the yielding word inside the French seas

parts.note: mers is French for seas
to cede is to yield

explanation.surface: A multinational must give ground in overseas waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercedes-Benz is a carmaker trading worldwide, a global firm.

clue.text: Victim pens poison mail in scholar's last exam

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the victim word surrounds the rest

parts.note: prey is a victim of a predator

indicators.note: poison says the following letters are spoiled into a new order
last takes the final letter of the scholar word

explanation.surface: A victim sends toxic letters during a student's final test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poison' is the anagram signal for the two words after it; 'pens' means encloses, as a pen holds sheep, so the victim wraps everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelim is an early, qualifying exam, the shortened form of this word.

clue.text: Prompt note should stop 20

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the note goes inside the other word

parts.note: 20 refers to the answer to 20 across
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A memo ought to halt an earlier entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is a nudge or cue, a prompt to act.

clue.text: Surveyed damaged ship, fully ready for report

indicators.note: for report says the spoken sound of the words gives the answer

parts.note: a wreck is a damaged ship; keyed up means fully ready, tense

explanation.surface: Inspected a ruined vessel, all set to write up findings.
explanation.walkthrough: To recce (reccy) is British military slang for reconnoitre.
explanation.definitionFit: To recce is to reconnoitre, so to have scouted an area.

clue.text: Soldiers failing to finish course?

indicators.note: the soldiers word does not reach its final letter

parts.note: a regiment is a unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops who drop out before completing their training.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'course' means a course of treatment or diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet or treatment.

clue.text: More suitable mass invention welcomed by visionary

indicators.note: welcomed by puts the following words inside the visionary

parts.note: a seer is a visionary prophet
a lie is an invention, a fabrication

explanation.surface: A prophet embracing a big fabrication is said to be more fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means proper or fitting, so this comparative means more appropriate.

clue.text: Submit 5 that is disappearing

indicators.note: disappearing removes the letters for that is from the other answer

parts.note: 5 refers to the answer to 5 down
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Hand over the fifth item, which is vanishing.
explanation.walkthrough: From REINDEER, the I and one E go, leaving RENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To render an account is to submit it, hand it over.

clue.text: Turkey, one having head and tail removed

indicators.note: the first word loses its head and the second its tail

parts.note: a unit is one
with means having, as in a man with a hat

explanation.surface: A turkey prepared by cutting off its head and tail.
explanation.walkthrough: UNIT loses its U and WITH loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is slang for a fool or a flop; a dimwit is such a fool.

clue.text: Fine shelter

definitions.meaning: at Oxford a penalty imposed on a student for breaking etiquette
a small fort or earthwork protection, also an old word for a head covering

explanation.definitionFit: Sconce names both an Oxford forfeit and a small defensive fortification.

clue.text: From which you might take off warm and dry little piece of rag?

definitions.text: From which you might take off

parts.note: to air laundry is to warm and dry it
a strip is a narrow piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Drying a scrap of cloth before taking it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests undressing, but here it is a plane leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is where aircraft lift off the ground.

clue.text: Smoke rising from Lake Erie

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fumes ascend over one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads upwards; the hidden run sits inside 'from Lake Erie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reek is an old and Scots word for smoke or fumes.

clue.text: Getting these two chaps out makes you exhausted

parts.note: two men's names, Peter and Ed
the second name, Ed

explanation.surface: Seeing off a pair of blokes wears you out.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus 'out' gives the phrase meaning dwindled away, so 'out' sits with the definition sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to run down and stop, so used up or spent.

clue.text: Reportedly imagines an English town

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for imagines is given as spoken

parts.note: devises means thinks up, imagines

explanation.surface: Someone is said to dream up a place in England.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVIZES is a market town in Wiltshire, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Devizes is a historic market town in Wiltshire, one English town.
